subject: Cooking
title: Wooden Cutting Boards vs. Plastic: The Surprise
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Wooden Cutting Boards vs. Plastic: The Surprise.

hook.text: Conventional wisdom says plastic cutting boards are more hygienic than wood. Research says the opposite.

buildup.text: UC Davis food scientist Dean Cliver tested both materials extensively in the 1990s.

discovery.text: Bacteria placed on wood were pulled below the surface and died. On plastic, they survived in knife scars.

twist.text: Scratched plastic boards harbor bacteria that survive dishwasher cycles — wood's natural properties kill them.

climax.text: Wood contains antimicrobial tannins and its porous structure traps and dehydrates bacteria effectively.

punchline.text: The 'unsanitary' cutting board turned out to be the safe one.

quiz.question: What happens to bacteria on wooden cutting boards according to research?
options: They're pulled below the surface and die

details.summary: The surprising finding that plastic cutting boards may be less hygienic than wood overturned decades of conventional kitchen wisdom. Knife-scarred plastic creates bacterial havens, while wood's porous surface actively kills bacteria trapped in its grain.
details.whyItMatters: This reversal illustrates how kitchen advice sometimes rests on untested assumptions. Actual laboratory testing showed the opposite of what authorities had recommended for years.
takeaways: Knife scars in plastic create bacterial colonies resistant to washing
Wood's porous grain traps then kills bacteria through desiccation
The safest choice is replacing worn boards of any material regularly

faq.question: Should I throw away my plastic cutting boards?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. New plastic boards are perfectly sanitary. The problem develops as knife cuts create grooves that trap bacteria. Replace plastic boards when they become visibly scarred and cannot be cleaned effectively.

faq.question: Which cutting board material is best overall?
faq.answer: The best board is the one you clean properly and replace when worn. Hardwoods like maple are excellent. Rubber composite boards combine durability with easy cleaning. The key factors are knife scar resistance, ease of cleaning, and regular replacement rather than material alone.
